lesson_title: The Year in Shapes, Data and Measures
hook_text: A rectangle has four sides and four corners. So it has four lines of symmetry, right? Fold it and see.
clip_script: Class trip near Knysna. The stop sign at the gate: 8 sides, an octagon. The cooler box: a rectangular prism, 6 faces. Picnic tiles: no gaps, no overlaps. Now the puzzle. Fold a rectangle across the middle: it matches. The other way: it matches. Along the diagonal? The corners stick out. Only 2 lines of symmetry. A square has 4. Survey: swings 12, slides 8, picnic 5, soccer 15, total 40. Bus: 08:15 to 10:40, 2 hours 25 minutes. Garden fence: 8 plus 5 plus 8 plus 5, 26 metres. Describe it, check it, give it a unit.
visual_style: Whiteboard rectangle and square folding along each line; a bar graph rising from 0; a clock jumping 2 hours then 25 minutes; a fence drawn around a garden.
mood: Energetic recap with a fold-it puzzle.
pacing: The symmetry puzzle, quick stops at shapes, data and time, then the fence and the three habits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a one-page map of the year's shape, data and measurement facts before the test.
